- Assessment summary from transcript:

- DDx integration (consistent items only):
  - Migraine — high likelihood: unilateral, throbbing, severe pain; family history supports diagnosis.
  - Cervicogenic headache / tension-type — moderate likelihood: posterior occipital location compatible; lack of neck pain or clear movement triggers reduces likelihood.
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — low likelihood: new severe headache raises consideration, but absence of thunderclap onset, meningism, vomiting, LOC or focal signs reduces likelihood.
- Contradictions/unsupported suggestions: None noted between transcript and DDx (alignment present)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine (new-onset primary headache) — High likelihood
  - Justification: Unilateral left posterior throbbing pain, severe (8/10), family history of migraine; absence of systemic or focal neurological signs.
- Cervicogenic headache / tension-type headache — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Posterior/occipital location compatible with cervicogenic origin; tension-type common and can impair function. Lack of neck pain or movement-provoked symptoms reduces certainty.
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — Low likelihood
  - Justification: New severe headache could raise concern; opposing evidence includes gradual build-up rather than thunderclap onset, no meningism, no vomiting, no focal signs.
